newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

In answer to a question, spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said it had not been possible for the Commission to make a new proposal on anti-dumping duties on cotton imports from several Asian countries. Van der Pas said the unananimity needed to call a new Council meeting on the issue, as requested by Commission President Jacques Santer, had not been reached on Tuesday in The Hague.
Van der Pas added that the Commission would immediately open a procedure if a new complaint was lodged.

Van der Pas said the Commission would publish the results of the Agenda 2000 review on July 16, 1997, notably its opinions accession applications, the financial perspectives after 1999 and the revision of internal policies after enlargement.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/424: Results of the consultation on a numbering policy for telecommunication services in Europe.
- IP/97/425: President Santer nominates the members of the second Competitiveness Advisory Group (CAG II).

- IP/97/426: State Aid: Austria - The Commission does not approve most of the state aid proposal by the Austrian authorities in favour of Hoffmann-La Roche for the production of Orlistat, a new anti-obesity drug.
- Communication on fighting corruption in the EU.
- Communication from Commissioner Anita Gradin to the Commission on the Communication on fighting corruption in the EU.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Energy and industry No 1997-8: Electricity prices for EU industry on 1 January 1997: downward trend.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Energy and industry No 1997-9: Gas prices for EU households on 1 January 1997: upward trend.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Economy and finance No 1997-15: Government and private sector investment in the EU 1980-1995.
